key_claims: Young P301S tau transgenic mice and wild-type mice seeded with human tau fibrils displayed locus coeruleus hyperexcitability alongside reduced low-threshold potassium current density.
Single-cell expression profiling showed increased stress-associated genes and reduced potassium-channel gene expression, including Kcnq3 and Kcnd1, in locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons.

Targeting potassium channels via chronic treatment with the Kv7 opener retigabine attenuated AT8-positive tau burden and was associated with higher TH-positive neuronal density after unilateral tau seeding.
limitations: The findings are restricted to mouse models and in vitro/ex vivo electrophysiological and pharmacological assays.
Single-cell RNA sequencing profiling changes were exploratory and present candidate mechanisms rather than established clinical markers.
The study did not evaluate human clinical outcomes or long-term safety of chronic Kv7 activation.
what_not_to_say: Do not claim that retigabine or Kv7 activation is a proven clinical treatment or cure for Alzheimer's disease in humans.
Do not state as fact that potassium channel dysfunction directly causes human cognitive decline based solely on mouse model data.
Do not imply that surrogate biomarker measurements reflect tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
